Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 11, verse 2:

﴿That you worship not﴾ i.e., with "an" (that), and the sense is: "This is a Book, [stating] that you worship not ﴿except Allah﴾."

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 11, verse 3:

﴿And﴾ [that] ﴿seek forgiveness from your Lord﴾, i.e., for your past sins, ﴿then repent to Him﴾ from what follows (al-mustani'afa, i.e., future sins), whenever they occur. ﴿He will let you enjoy a good provision﴾, bestowing upon you sustenance and abundance, ﴿until a specified term﴾, the term of death. ﴿And He will give every doer of virtue his virtue﴾, i.e., He will give everyone whose good deeds outweigh his bad deeds his virtue, meaning Paradise, which is the bounty of God, glorified is He. ﴿But if you turn away﴾, i.e., turn away from faith, ﴿then indeed I fear for you the punishment of a great day﴾, which is the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 11, verse 5:

﴿Ah, indeed they fold their chests﴾ It was revealed concerning a group of the polytheists who said: "When we close our doors, let down our curtains, wrap ourselves in our garments, and fold our chests over enmity toward Muhammad (ﷺ), how will our Lord know?" Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 11, verse 45:

﴿And Noah called out to his Lord and said, "My Lord, indeed my son is from my family, and indeed Your promise is the truth"﴾ [the son is] Kan'an; ﴿and Your promise is the truth﴾ [meaning:] You promised me that You would save me and my family, i.e., so save him from drowning; ﴿and You are the most just of judges﴾ [meaning:] "the most equitable of those who are equitable."

"He said, 'O Noah, indeed he is not of your family' — those whom I promised to save — 'indeed, his deed is unrighteous.' That is: your request to Me that I save a disbeliever is an unrighteous deed. It was also said that the meaning is: indeed your son has an unrighteous deed. 'So do not ask Me about that of which you have no knowledge.' This is because Noah did not know that his asking his Lord for the salvation of his son was forbidden to him while he persisted in disbelief, until Allah the Glorious informed him of that. The meaning is: 'So do not ask Me about that of which you have no knowledge regarding the permissibility of asking it.' 'Indeed, I admonish you' — I forbid you — 'lest you be among the ignorant' — among the sinners. So Noah, peace be upon him, made excuse when Allah the Glorious informed him that it was not permissible for him to ask that, and said:"

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 11, verse 47:

﴿My Lord, I seek refuge in You from asking You about that of which I have no knowledge. And unless You forgive me and have mercy on me, I will be among the losers.﴾ (my ignorance) ﴿And have mercy on me, I will be among the losers.﴾

"It was said: O Noah, descend ﴿with peace﴾ from the ship to the earth, with safety. And it was said: with a greeting from Us, ﴿and blessings upon you﴾. That is because he became the father of mankind, since all who remained were from his offspring, ﴿and upon nations from those with you﴾, that is, from their children and descendants, and they are the believers and the people of felicity until the Day of Resurrection. ﴿And nations We will provide for﴾ in this world, meaning: the disbelieving nations from his descendants until the Day of Resurrection."

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 11, verse 49:

﴿That﴾ is the story I have told you, ﴿of the tidings of the unseen﴾, the reports of what was hidden from you and from your people. ﴿So be patient﴾, just as Noah was patient with the harm of his people. ﴿Indeed, the outcome is for the God-fearing﴾: in the end, victory belongs to you and to your people, just as it belonged to the believers of Noah's people.
"And His saying: ﴿You are but inventors of falsehood﴾ — you are only liars in your associating idols (with Allah)."

Her "And He will send the sky upon you in abundant rain" ... Let me give the translation properly:

"And [He said]: ﴿He will send the sky upon you in abundance of rain﴾, meaning abundant in outpouring, [i.e.] the rain, ﴿and will add strength to your strength﴾, meaning wealth and children. Allah, glorified is He, had withheld the rain from them for three years and had made the wombs of their women barren. So Hud said to them: If you believe, Allah, glorified is He, will revive your lands and provide you with wealth and children."

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 11, verse 53:

﴿They said﴾ denying his prophethood: ﴿O Hud, you have brought us no clear proof﴾ no evident argument.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 11, verse 54:

And His saying: ﴿Has smitten you﴾, meaning, has befallen you and touched you, ﴿some of our gods with evil﴾, meaning with madness, so that it has corrupted your intellect. So what appears of their defect is the change that has come upon your intellect. ﴿He said﴾, the Prophet of Allah, peace be upon him, at that point: ﴿Indeed, I call Allah to witness, and bear witness yourselves, that I am free from what you associate [with Him]﴾, meaning: if you hold that the idols have punished me for my criticism of them, then I now increase my criticism of them.

Their statement: "So scheme against me all together" (Qur'an 11:55): devise plots against me, you and your idols together in your enmity toward me, "then give me no respite" (Qur'an 11:55): do not delay me.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 11, verse 57:

﴿Then if you turn away﴾: "tatawallaw" means: you turn away from what I have called you to, namely faith. ﴿then I have conveyed to you that with which I was sent to you﴾: the proof has been established against you by my conveying (the message). ﴿And my Lord will replace you with another people﴾: that is, He will bring after you others who are more obedient to Him than you. ﴿And you will not harm Him﴾ by your turning away ﴿at all﴾; rather, you harm only yourselves. ﴿Indeed, my Lord is, over all things﴾ of the deeds of the servants ﴿Guardian﴾, until He recompenses them for them.

﴿And when Our command came﴾ to destroy ʿĀd, ﴿We saved Hūd and those who believed with him by a mercy from Us﴾ in that We guided them to faith and protected them from disbelief, ﴿and We saved them from a severe punishment﴾, meaning: the punishment with which those who disbelieved were punished.

This is Surah Hud, verse 59. Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz):

﴿And that was ʿĀd﴾. He means: the tribe. ﴿They denied the signs of their Lord﴾: they called them lies and did not acknowledge them. ﴿And disobeyed His messengers﴾: he means Hud, peace be upon him, because whoever denies one messenger has disbelieved in all the messengers. ﴿And followed the command of every obstinate tyrant﴾. The common people followed the chiefs. And ʿanīd (obstinate): one who opposes you by disputing.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 11, verse 60:

﴿And they were pursued by a curse in this world﴾: they were followed by a curse that overtook them and went along with them. ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection﴾: that is, and on the Day of Resurrection too, as He said: ﴿They were cursed in this world and the Hereafter.﴾ ﴿Indeed, ʿAd disbelieved in their Lord.﴾ It was said: in their Lord; and it was said: they disbelieved the blessing of their Lord. ﴿Ah, away with ʿAd!﴾ He means: they were removed far from the mercy of God, the Exalted.

Al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on Surah 11, verse 61:

And His saying: ﴿He it is who produced you﴾, that is: created you ﴿from the earth﴾, from Adam, and Adam was created from the dust of the earth. ﴿And made you inhabit it﴾, that is, made you its settlers (ʿammarān, plural of ʿammār, those who populate and cultivate it).

﴿They said, "O Salih, you were among us a man of hope before this."﴾ That is because Salih, peace be upon him, used to turn away from their religion and denounce their idols, and they had hoped he would return to the religion of his tribe. When he openly called them to worship Allah, the Exalted, they claimed that their hope in him had been cut off. As for His saying ﴿mureeb﴿, it means one who causes doubt (rayb).

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 11, verse 63:

﴿He said: "O my people, have you considered...﴾ the verse. He means: Have you informed me who will support me against Allah, that is, who will protect me from the punishment of Allah if I disobey Him after a clear proof from my Lord and a blessing? ﴿Then you would not increase me except in loss.﴾ That is: you do not increase me, by your argument of worshipping the idols of your fathers and your saying: ﴿Do you order us to abandon what our fathers worshipped?﴾ except by attributing loss to you. That is: whenever you offer an excuse, it increases you in loss. It was also said that the meaning of the verse is: you increase me only in loss, if you are my helpers. The word "takhsir" (causing loss, ruin) means misguidance and being removed from good.
Their commentary on His words, ﴿Enjoy yourselves in your homes﴾, meaning: live in your lands ﴿for three days. That is a promise﴾ of punishment ﴿not to be denied﴾, meaning: not a lie.

And His saying: ﴿And from the disgrace of that day﴾, meaning: We saved them from the punishment that destroyed their people, and from the disgrace that clung to them, and the shame that remained among them, related from them. So the waw in ﴿and from﴾ is coordinated (nasaq) with an omitted element, which is the punishment.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 11, verse 67:

﴿And the seizure of those who did wrong was the Blast.﴾ When they awoke on the fourth day, there came upon them a blast from the sky, in which was the sound of every thunderbolt and the sound of everything on the earth, and their hearts split apart within their chests.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 11, verse 69:

﴿And certainly Our messengers came to Ibrahim (Abraham) with the good tidings﴾, meaning: the angels who came to ﴿Ibrahim﴾ (peace be upon him) in the form of guests, ﴿with the good tidings﴾, the glad tidings of a son. ﴿They said: "Peace"﴾, meaning: they said, "Peace [be upon you]." ﴿He said: "Peace"﴾, meaning: "Upon you be peace." ﴿Then he did not delay, but brought a roasted calf﴾, meaning: roasted.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 11, verse 70:

﴿So when he saw their hands not reaching toward it﴾ toward the calf, ﴿he disliked them﴾ he disapproved of them, ﴿and he sensed fear of them﴾ he concealed within himself fear of them, and he did not feel secure that they had come for a trial, since they did not partake of his food. Then, when they saw the sign of fear on his face, ﴿they said: Fear not, for we have been sent to the people of Lot﴾ with punishment.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 11, verse 71:

﴿And his wife﴾ Sarah was ﴿standing﴾ behind the curtain, eavesdropping on the messengers. ﴿She laughed﴾ out of joy at the security. They said: ﴿Indeed, We have been sent to the people of Lot.﴾ That was because she had become frightened, just as Ibrahim (peace be upon him) had become frightened. So it was said to her: "O laughing one, you will bear a boy." That is His saying: ﴿So We gave her good tidings of Ishaq, and after Ishaq, Ya'qub.﴾ That is, after him, ﴿Ya'qub﴾ (peace be upon them both). That was because they gave her the good news that she would live until she saw the children of her son.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 11, verse 72:

﴿She said: "Woe to me! Shall I give birth while I am an old woman, and this, my husband, is an old man?"﴾ She was ninety-nine years old, and he was one hundred and twelve years old. ﴿Indeed, this is﴾ the thing you mention, the bearing of a child in my old age and the old age of my husband, ﴿truly a wondrous thing﴾, astonishing.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 11, verse 73:

﴿They said: "Do you wonder at the command of Allah?"﴾ That is, the decree and destiny of Allah. ﴿"The mercy of Allah and His blessings be upon you, O people of the house"﴾ That is, the house of Ibrahim, peace be upon him. Among those blessings was that the tribes (al-asbat) and all the prophets were from Ibrahim and Sarah. This was a supplication from the angels for them. And His saying: ﴿"Indeed, He is Praiseworthy, Glorious"﴾ That is, Mahmud (praiseworthy), Majid (generous, noble).

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 11, verse 74:

﴿When the fear had left Abraham and the good tidings had come to him, he began to argue with Us concerning the people of Lot.﴾ That is: he came forward and began to argue with Our messengers ﴿concerning the people of Lot.﴾ The reason was that when they said to Abraham, peace be upon him, ﴿Indeed, We are going to destroy the people of this town,﴾ he said to them: "Do you think that if there are fifty Muslims in it, you would destroy them?" They said: "No." He said: "Then forty?" They said: "No." He kept reducing the number until he said: "Then one?" They said: "No." So he argued against them on behalf of Lot, and ﴿he said: "Indeed, Lot is in it." They said: "We know best who is in it"﴾ (the verse). This is the meaning of his argument. At that point the angels said:
"O Ibrahim, turn away from this" — the dispute — and they left him and came to the town of the people of Lut. This is what is meant by His saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 11, verse 77:

﴿And when Our messengers came to Lot, he was distressed on their account and felt helpless for them﴾. He was grieved at their coming, because he saw them in the most beautiful form, so he feared for them from his people, and he knew that he would need to defend them. They had come to him in the form of guests. ﴿And he was constrained for them, and said, "This is a trying day"﴾, meaning: his chest was constricted (dhar'an, i.e. "constraint of chest"). ﴿This is a trying day﴾: difficult and severe. When his people learned of the coming of men of handsome faces as guests of Lot, they made for his house, and that is His saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 11, verse 78:

﴿And his people came hastening toward him﴾, that is, they rushed toward him. ﴿And before this﴾, that is, before their coming to Lut, ﴿they had been doing evil deeds﴾, meaning: their abominable act. ﴿He said: O my people, these are my daughters﴾, I will marry them to you, ﴿they are purer for you﴾ than marrying men. He wanted to protect his guests with his daughters. ﴿So fear Allah and do not disgrace me concerning my guests﴾, do not humiliate me before them, for if they attacked his guests with what is hateful, disgrace would befall him. ﴿Is there not among you a man of sound judgment﴾, one who enjoins what is good and forbids what is evil.

﴿They said: "You certainly know that we have no right to your daughters."﴾ They are not wives for us, so that we would have a claim to them. ﴿"And you certainly know what we desire."﴾ That is: we desire men, not women.

"He said, 'If only I had against you some power, or could take refuge in some strong support!'" — that is, "If only I had with me a group stronger than you by which I could overpower you, or could join a strong pillar, a clan that would protect me and support me, I would have stood between you and disobedience." Then, when the angels saw that...

"They said, 'O Lut, we are messengers of your Lord; they will never reach you. So set out with your family in a part of the night, and let none of you turn back to look, except your wife; indeed, what strikes them will strike her too. Indeed, their appointed time is the morning. Is not the morning near?'" — [translated as the passage gives it: see below]

Here is the faithful translation of the passage:

﴿They said, "O Lut, indeed we are messengers from your Lord; they will never reach you with harm. So set out with your family in a part of the night.﴾ (i.e., in the darkness of the night) ﴿And let not any one of you look back﴾ (i.e., no one should look behind him when he leaves his town) ﴿except your wife﴾ — so do not travel with her; leave her with her people, for her inclination is toward them — ﴿indeed, she will be struck by what strikes them﴾ of the punishment. ﴿Indeed, their appointed time is the morning.﴾ Lut said: "I wish it were sooner than that; rather, now, O Jibril!" They said to him: "Is not the morning near?"

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 11, verse 82:

﴿So when Our command came﴾, meaning Our punishment, ﴿We made its highest part its lowest﴾. The reason was that Jibril (peace be upon him) inserted his wing beneath it until he uprooted it, ascended with it to the sky, and then overturned it toward the earth. ﴿And We rained upon it stones of sijjil﴾, before its overturning toward the earth, ﴿of sijjil﴾, meaning of clay that has been baked, baked until it became like brick (ājurr). It is sanj-kil in Persian, which was Arabicized (fa-ʿurrib). ﴿Layered﴾, meaning one following another.

﴿Marked﴾, distinguished by a sign showing that they were not stones of the people of this world, ﴿with your Lord﴾, in His treasuries, from which nothing is disposed of except by His will, ﴿and they are not far from the wrongdoers﴾. That is, the disbelievers of Quraysh, whom He frightens with them.

And to Madyan [We sent] their brother Shu'ayb. We have already mentioned the explanation of this verse in Surat al-A'raf. And His saying: ﴿Indeed, I see you in prosperity﴾ means: in blessing and abundance. He says: What need do you have for short-measuring, with what Allah, glorified is He, has bestowed upon you of wealth and low prices? ﴿And indeed, I fear for you the punishment of an encompassing day﴾ He warns them of a punishment that will encircle them, so that not one of them will escape.
﴿And O my people, give full measure and weight with justice﴾ — complete them with fairness.

"What Allah leaves for you" (baqiyyat Allah) means: what Allah preserves for you after you give full measure and weight, is better for you than cheating (al-bakhs), that is, than hastening gain by it, "if you are believers," meaning affirming His blessings. He made belief a condition because they would only recognize the truth of what he says if they were believers. "And I am not a guardian over you" means: I have not been commanded to fight you or to compel you to believe.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 11, verse 87:

﴿They said, "O Shu'ayb, does your prayer command you that we abandon what our fathers worshipped?"﴾ They mean: your religion commands you. That is: "Is it in your religion that such a command is found?" ﴿Or that we should do with our wealth what we wish﴾ — such as defrauding and wronging, and diminishing the measure and the scale. ﴿Indeed, you are the forbearing, the discerning﴾ — that is: the foolish, the ignorant. And they said: "the forbearing, the discerning" in the manner of mockery.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 11, verse 88:

﴿He said: "O my people, have you considered"﴾ i.e., have you informed yourselves, ﴿if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord﴾ i.e., manifest proof and argument from my Lord, ﴿and He has provided me from Himself with good provision﴾ i.e., lawful provision. This was because he had much wealth. The answer to "if" (in) is omitted, meaning: if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord, and He has provided me with lawful wealth, would I follow misguidance, diminish (people's measures) and cheat in measure? He intends: indeed Allah the Exalted has enriched him with lawful wealth. ﴿And I do not intend to oppose you in that which I forbid you from.﴾ i.e., I do not forbid you from something and then engage in it myself; rather, I choose for you what I choose for myself. ﴿I intend only reform﴾ what I intend ﴿but reform﴾ between me and you, by your worshipping Allah alone and doing what one who fears Allah does, ﴿as much as I am able.﴾ i.e., to the extent of my capacity and my capacity for conveying and warning. Then he informed them that neither he nor anyone else is able to obey except by the success granted by Allah, the Glorified, so he said: ﴿And my success is not except through Allah. Upon Him I have relied, and to Him I turn back in repentance.﴾ i.e., I return at the appointed time.

And O my people, let not my opposition (shiqaq) cause you to incur [the same fate]: "لا يجرمنكم" means "let not my dissension and enmity earn you" [anything]. "أن يصيبكم" [that it should befall you] — the punishment of this world — "مثل ما أصاب قوم نوح" [like what befell the people of Noah] — from drowning — "أو قوم هود" [or the people of Hud] — from the barren wind — "أو قوم صالح" [or the people of Salih] — from the earthquake and the blast.

"وما قوم لوط منكم ببعيد" [And the people of Lut are not far from you] — in time, between you and them; and their destruction was the nearest of the destructions that they knew of.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 11, verse 90:

﴿And seek forgiveness from your Lord﴾: ask Him for forgiveness. ﴿Then turn to Him in repentance﴾: draw near to Him through repentance. ﴿Indeed, my Lord is Merciful﴾: toward His friends (awliya'). ﴿Loving﴾ (wadud): loving toward them.

﴿They said: "O Shu'ayb, we do not understand much of what you say"﴾ — that is, we do not grasp it. ﴿Much of what you say﴾ — meaning: its soundness; they mean what he mentions of tawhid (the oneness of God), resurrection (al-ba'th) and gathering (al-nushur). ﴿And indeed we see you among us as weak﴾ — because he was blind. ﴿Were it not for your clan (rahtuk)﴾ — your tribe. ﴿We would have stoned you﴾ — we would have killed you. ﴿And you are not mighty against us﴾ — not protected.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 11, verse 92:

﴿He said: "O my people, is my clan more esteemed by you than God?"﴾ He means: "Is my protection from you greater than God's?" As if he were saying: "Your guarding me for the sake of God is more fitting than guarding me for the sake of my clan." ﴿And you have taken Him behind your backs as something cast away.﴾ You have cast Him behind your backs and refrained from killing me out of fear of my people, while God is more mighty and greater than all His creation. ﴿Indeed, my Lord is encompassing of what you do.﴾ He is Knowing of the deeds of the servants, so that He will recompense them for them. Then he threatened them, saying:

O my people, act according to your position; indeed I am acting according to mine, in obedience to Allah. You will soon know who will receive a punishment that will disgrace him and who is a liar among us. And wait; indeed I am waiting with you as an observer. Wait for the punishment from Allah, the Exalted; indeed I am awaiting mercy from Allah, the Exalted.
Wa-qawluhu: ﴿Akhadhat alladhina zalamu al-sayhah﴾ — "And the Cry seized those who had done wrong." Jibril cried out at them with one cry, and they died in their places.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 11, verse 95:

﴿Unquestionably, away with Midian!﴾ That is: they have been removed far from the mercy of Allah, the Exalted.
And We certainly sent Musa with Our signs (ayat), meaning: the Torah and the rulings Allah revealed in it. And a clear authority (sultan mubin), meaning: a manifest proof, and it is the staff.
﴿And the command of Pharaoh was not rightly guided.﴾ Not leading to good.

Translation:

﴿He will go before his people﴾ leading them to the Fire, and this is His saying: ﴿and lead them into the Fire﴾, that is, He will cause them to enter the Fire. ﴿And wretched is the watering-place to which they are brought﴾, that is, the place of entry into which they are led.

**Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 11, verse 99:**

﴿And they were followed in this﴾ (world) by ﴿a curse﴾. He means: the drowning. ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection﴾. He means: and a curse on the Day of Resurrection, which is the punishment of Jahannam (Hell). ﴿Evil is the gift that is given.﴾ He means: a curse after a curse.

And His saying: ﴿Of them some are standing and some are mown down﴾ — meaning: of the towns that were destroyed, some have their walls still standing, and some are uprooted and swept away by the earth, their traces wiped out.

And We did not wrong them (by the punishment and destruction), but they wronged themselves (by disbelief and disobedience). So their gods which they invoked besides Allah did not avail them (did not benefit them and did not ward off from them) anything, and they added nothing to them except ruin (their worship of them added nothing but calamity, destruction and loss).

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 11, verse 102:

﴿And so⦆ — as We have mentioned concerning the destruction of past nations — ﴿is the seizing of your Lord⦆ — with punishment — ﴿when He seizes the towns while they are wrongdoing⦆ — meaning: their people.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 11, verse 103:

﴿Indeed, in that⦆ means: in what has been mentioned of the punishment of the former nations, ﴿is a sign⦆ a lesson ﴿for those who fear the punishment of the Hereafter. That is a Day for which mankind will be gathered⦆ because all creation will be brought together and assembled for that Day, ﴿and that is a Day witnessed⦆ by the righteous and the wicked alike.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 11, verse 104:

﴿And We do not delay it﴾ — and We do not delay that Day, so that We would not establish it upon you, ﴿except for a limited term﴾ — for a known, appointed time, and no one knows it except Allah, glorified is He.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 11, verse 105:

﴿On the day it comes﴾, that day, ﴿no soul will speak except by His permission. Among them will be the wretched and the happy﴾. So among the souls on that day there are the wretched and the happy.

﴿As for those who are wretched, they will be in the Fire, where for them is groaning and wailing.﴾ These two are among the sounds of the distressed and the grieved. The zafir (groaning) is like the first braying of a donkey, and the shahiq (wailing) is its last, when it repeats it within the chest.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 11, verse 107:

﴿Abiding therein for as long as the heavens and the earth endure﴾: forever. This is among the expressions of perpetuity. ﴿Except what your Lord wills﴾: that He would bring them out, but He does not will that. The meaning is: if He willed not to make them eternal, He would have decreed it. It is also said: ﴿except what your Lord wills﴾ means: except the length of their stay in this world, in the barzakh (the intermediate state), and in standing for the reckoning; then they will go to the Fire forever.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 11, verse 108:

And His saying: ﴿a gift never cut off﴾, meaning: uninterrupted (maqtu').

﴿So do not be﴾ O Muhammad ﴿in doubt﴾ (shakk) ﴿about what these worship﴾ i.e., about the state of what they worship, that it neither harms nor benefits. ﴿They worship only as their fathers worshipped before﴾ i.e., like the worship of their fathers. He means: they worship idols by way of blind imitation (taqlid), just as their fathers worshipped. ﴿And indeed, We will give them their share﴾ of the punishment ﴿undiminished.﴾

This verse is a consolation to the Prophet (ﷺ) and a comfort to him regarding the disagreement of Moses' people over their Book. ﴿And We certainly gave Moses the Book, but it was disputed about.﴾ ﴿And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord﴾ (delaying the punishment from your people), ﴿the matter would have been decided between them﴾ (their punishment would have been hastened and the matter concluded). ﴿And indeed, they are in disquieting doubt about it﴾ (about the Qur'an), ﴿causing suspicion﴾ (producing doubt).

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 11, verse 111:

﴿And indeed, each﴾ of the righteous and the wicked, the believer and the disbeliever, ﴿[will be those whom] your Lord will surely repay in full for their deeds﴾. That is, ﴿la-ma﴾ means: "la" with "man" (those who), according to the saying of al-Farra' (al-Farra' [d. 207 AH], the grammarian), and according to the saying of the Basrans, "ma" is additional (ziyadah), and the meaning is: "And indeed, each ﴿will surely be repaid by your Lord for their deeds﴾." That is: it will certainly be fulfilled for them, the recompense of their deeds.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 11, verse 112:

﴿So be upright﴾ in acting by the command of your Lord and in calling to Him, ﴿as you have been commanded﴾ in the Qur'an, ﴿and those who have turned back with you﴾ in repentance, meaning: his companions. That is, let them also be upright in what they have been commanded, ﴿and do not transgress﴾: be humble before God and do not act arrogantly toward anyone. ﴿Indeed, He is Seeing of what you do﴾: the deeds of the children of Adam are not hidden from Him.

**Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on Surah 11, verse 113:**

﴿And do not incline toward those who wronged, lest the Fire touch you, and you have no protectors other than Allah; then you will not be helped.﴾ Do not flatter them, and do not approve of their deeds, meaning the disbelievers. ﴿Lest the Fire touch you﴾ means its scorching blaze reaches you. ﴿And you have no protectors other than Allah﴾ means no one who can prevent you from the punishment of Allah. ﴿Then you will not be helped﴾ is an *istinaf* (a resumptive clause, a new independent sentence that begins afresh).

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 11, verse 114:

﴿And establish the prayer at the two ends of the day﴾ — that is, at dawn (al-subh) and at sunset (al-maghrib), ﴿and in the first hours of the night﴾ — that is, the prayer of ʿishaʾ (the night prayer), near the beginning of the night. Al-zulaf is the first hours of the night. It has also been said: the prayer at the two ends of the day is the prayer of dawn, the midday prayer (al-zuhr) and the afternoon prayer (al-ʿasr), while the maghrib and ʿishaʾ prayers are from the prayer of the zulaf of the night. ﴿Indeed, good deeds erase bad deeds﴾ — indeed, the five prayers expiate the sins that lie between them when the major sins are avoided. ﴿That is a reminder﴾ — that is, this is an admonition ﴿for those who remember﴾.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 11, verse 115:

﴿And be patient﴾ over the prayer, ﴿for indeed Allah does not waste the reward of the good-doers﴾, meaning:

the ones who pray

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 11, verse 116:

﴿Why were there not among the generations before you﴾ i.e., were there not among them ﴿people of a remnant﴾ of religion, distinction and excellence ﴿who forbade corruption on earth﴾ — [forbade] shirk and transgression against the rights of God and disobedience — ﴿except a few﴾, but only a few ﴿of those whom We saved from among them﴾, and they were the followers of the prophets and the people of truth who forbade corruption. ﴿And those who did wrong pursued what they had been given of luxury therein﴾: they preferred worldly pleasures over the matter of the Hereafter, inclined toward this world, its wealth, and what they were given of its bounties.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 11, verse 117:

﴿And your Lord would never destroy the cities unjustly while their people were reforming﴾. That is: their people. ﴿Unjustly﴾: by polytheism. ﴿While their people were reforming﴾ among themselves. That is: it is not the way of the disbelievers, when they intend the truth in dealing with one another, that God sends down upon them the punishment of annihilation, as with the people of Lot, who were punished for sodomy, and the people of Shu'ayb, who were punished for cheating in measure.

And if your Lord had willed, He would have made mankind one community ﴿وَلَوْ شَاءَ رَبُّكَ لَجَعَلَ النَّاسَ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً﴾ — all of them Muslims — ﴿ولا يزالون مختلفين﴾ — they would continue to differ in religions.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 11, verse 119:

﴿Except those upon whom your Lord has mercy﴾, meaning: the people of the truth. ﴿And for that He created them﴾, meaning: He created the people of disagreement for disagreement, and the people of mercy for mercy.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 11, verse 120:

﴿And all that We relate to you of the news of the messengers﴾ means: all that you need of it. ﴿We relate to you﴾ that by which We make your heart firm, so as to increase you in certainty. ﴿And there has come to you in this﴾ means: in this surah ﴿the truth﴾, meaning: what has been mentioned of the stories of the prophets and their admonitions, and the mention of happiness and wretchedness. This is an honouring of this surah, because the truth has come in other surahs too. ﴿And an admonition and a reminder for the believers﴾ who take heed when they hear this surah and what befell the nations when they denied their prophets.
And say to those who do not believe: "Act according to your position" — a command of threat, i.e., do what you are doing.
﴿And wait﴾ for what Satan promises you, ﴿indeed we are waiting﴾ for what our Lord promises us of victory.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 11, verse 123:

﴿And to Allah belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth﴾, that is: the knowledge of what is hidden from the servants in them. ﴿And to Him the whole matter will be returned﴾ on the Day of Return, so that no one besides Him will have any command. ﴿And your Lord is not unaware of what you do﴾, that is: He will reward the doer of good for his good and the doer of evil for his evil.
